## Source discovery and audits

Five fresh source identities not previously recorded under those exact names were screened. Three received full source-specific audits before admission decisions:

1. **BIDICAM — Biblioteca Digital de Castilla-La Mancha** — full audit and admitted. Its first-party presentation says BIDICAM exists to preserve and provide open access to digitized bibliographic heritage in Castilla-La Mancha that is not subject to copyright, supports title/author and collection discovery, and permits full-document downloads in several formats. First-party search help and the historical-periodicals route were live. Safe admitted capability: exactly three first-party **link-only discovery** routes. The broader Patrimonio Digital host also contains other microsites and material with different rights histories, so no host-wide redistribution or harvesting permission was inferred.
2. **Galiciana — Patrimonio Digital de Galicia** — full audit and deferred. The Xunta de Galicia service is an aggregator and directory spanning participating memory institutions and OAI-PMH repositories across books, newspapers, archival material, photographs, maps, and other objects. That aggregation model does not establish one collection-wide object-reuse rule suitable for generic ingestion. Any future adapter must preserve institution/item rights, provenance, record/file identity, update/deletion, transport, pagination, and resource/failure semantics.
3. **DigiVatLib — Digital Vatican Library** — full audit and deferred for automated content ingestion. The current first-party manuscript viewer exposes IIIF and downloadable images, but displayed rights language says images are Copyright Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, free image use is limited to personal/study purposes, and printed or online publication requires permission. WebNR therefore did not mirror, harvest, or redistribute those images or manifests.
4. **BIVALDI — Biblioteca Valenciana Digital** — screened and deferred. The digital-library identity and cultural-heritage discovery value are established, but this bounded pass did not obtain sufficiently current first-party collection-wide reuse/access evidence to admit an automated source capability. A later audit may reconsider a link-only boundary from fresh first-party evidence.
5. **BiNaDi — Biblioteca Navarra Digital** — screened and deferred. Its current first-party OPAC and collection browsing are live, but this cycle did not establish a collection-wide automated reuse grant or the record/file/update contract needed for ingestion. No capability was inferred from public discoverability alone.

### Integrated source

- PR #189 added `public/sources/bidicam-castilla-la-mancha-digital-library-discovery-starter` with exactly three reviewed first-party routes: BIDICAM overview, first-party assisted catalog search, and BIDICAM historical-periodicals discovery.
- The source stores only WebNR-authored labels/descriptions and reviewed links. It does **not** harvest OAI, crawl result sets, download PDFs/images, extract OCR, mirror upstream metadata, proxy requests, forward credentials, or synchronize in the background.
- A richer BIDICAM adapter remains gated on explicit record/file identity, item-level rights and attribution, stable acquisition URLs, transport/CORS, robots/rate limits, pagination, update/deletion, encoding/OCR, resource/failure, and fixture evidence.
- This increases maintained source families from **36 to 37**.
